final_diagnosis.root_cause: The `currencyservice` deployment in the `boutique` namespace cannot start because its pod is stuck in `ErrImagePull` — Kubernetes is unable to pull the container image referenced in the pod spec. This is typically caused by an invalid image name/tag, a wrong registry path, or missing/incorrect imagePullSecrets.
final_diagnosis.report:
The `currencyservice` deployment in the `boutique` namespace cannot start because its pod is stuck in `ErrImagePull` — Kubernetes is unable to pull the container image referenced in the pod spec

## Findings
• Exactly one workload is failing in `boutique`: `currencyservice`.
• The failure mode is `ErrImagePull` (image-pull failure at the kubelet level), not a runtime crash, OOMKilled, or CrashLoopBackOff.
• The `currencyservice` deployment has zero available replicas (0/1 ready, 1 desired, 0 available).
• No restarts have occurred (RESTARTS=0), confirming the container never successfully started.
• All 10 other microservices in `boutique` (adservice, cartservice, checkoutservice, emailservice, frontend, paymentservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, redis-cart, shippingservice) are Running 1/1 with 0 restarts, making namespace/node/registry-wide issues unlikely.

*Non-Validated Claims (Inferred):*
• The exact failing image reference (likely a bad tag or typo in the image path) was not retrieved.
• Whether the failure is due to a missing imagePullSecret vs. a nonexistent tag vs. a private-registry auth error was not confirmed — the underlying kubelet error string was not observed.
• Whether this is a fresh rollout regression (deployment age of 37s is consistent but not confirmed against deployment history).

## Recommended Actions
• Run `kubectl describe pod currencyservice-b68d5576c-gbl9k -n boutique` and read the Events section to capture the exact image-pull error (e.g., `manifest unknown`, `unauthorized`, `repository does not exist`).
• Inspect the deployment's image: `kubectl get deploy currencyservice -n boutique -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[*].image}'` and compare against the expected image tag in the source manifest / Helm values / GitOps repo.
• If the tag is wrong/typo, fix it via `kubectl set image deploy/currencyservice -n boutique server=<correct-image:tag>` or revert with `kubectl rollout undo deploy/currencyservice -n boutique`.
• If the error is `unauthorized`/`denied`, verify `imagePullSecrets` on the pod spec / service account and confirm the secret exists with valid credentials (`kubectl get secret -n boutique`).
• Confirm the image exists in the registry (e.g., `crane manifest <image:tag>` or registry UI); push the missing tag if a CI/CD build was skipped.
• Watch `kubectl get pods -n boutique -w` until `currencyservice` becomes `1/1 Running`, and verify `checkoutservice`/`frontend` can reach it.
• Add a CI gate that fails the release if the referenced image tag is not present in the registry, to prevent recurrence.


*Cited Evidence:*
- Queries: GetAlerts, list eks pods, list eks deployments, get eks events, DescribeResource, GetAppYAML, GetErrorLogs, GetResources, GetServiceDependencies


Timing: 73s
